claims.text: The initial material is as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
Controlled introduction of porosity will reduce the density of HfMoTaTiZr.
Controlled porosity will not significantly compromise room-temperature mechanical performance.
Controlled porosity will not significantly compromise mechanical performance at temperatures up to 1000 °C.
A significant volume fraction of the strong HfMoTaTiZr phase will remain after porosity is introduced.
Retention of a significant volume fraction of HfMoTaTiZr may maintain alloy strength despite the porosity.
Pores may act as crack-arrest sites.
Porosity may improve the fracture toughness of HfMoTaTiZr.
The modified alloy will have a density below 10.0 g cm−3.
The modified alloy will retain a room-temperature yield strength above 1500 MPa.
The modified alloy will retain a yield strength above 800 MPa at 1000 °C.
The modified alloy will have fracture toughness equal to or greater than the as-cast baseline.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of 10.21 g cm−3.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a room-temperature yield strength of about 1600 MPa.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has an elevated-temperature yield strength of 855 MPa.
Mechanical performance is to be assessed under tensile loading from room temperature through 1000 °C.
The effects of porosity depend on pore size, distribution, and volume fraction.
Selective laser sintering or spark plasma sintering can be used to introduce controlled porosity into HfMoTaTiZr.
The hypothesis is rejected if a density reduction greater than 10% fails to maintain the specified yield-strength and fracture-toughness criteria.

contradictions.description: The predicted density target is merely below 10.0 g cm−3, approximately a 2.1% reduction from 10.21 g cm−3, whereas the rejection rule applies only when density falls by more than 10%. Thus failure to retain strength at the stated target density would not necessarily trigger rejection.
The rejection rule refers to specified fracture-toughness criteria, but the hypothesis supplies no quantitative toughness threshold or baseline toughness value.
